words: ذكر من معي وذكر من قبلي
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One possible sense is that the Quran and earlier prophetic revelation remind Muhammad's community and earlier peoples that divinity and worship belong only to God.
rows.anchor: أو أن ما في القرآن من الوحي النازل علي وهو ذكر من معي والوحي النازل على من سبقني من الأنبياء

words: أكثرهم لا يعلمون الحق فهم معرضون
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most cannot distinguish truth from falsehood, so they are not people who follow proof and instead turn away from truth and obedience to it.
rows.anchor: أكثرهم لا يميزون الحق من الباطل فليسوا من أهل التمييز الذين لا يتبعون إلا الدليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that every messenger received revelation confirming the preceding verse's remembrance of God's oneness and duty of worship also supports the second proposed sense of remembrance.
rows.anchor: تثبيت لما قيل في الآية السابقة إن الذكر يذكر توحيده ووجوب عبادته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The imperfect verb form conveys continuity in God's revelation to the messengers.
rows.anchor: وقوله { نوحي إليه } مفيد للاستمرار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to worship addresses the messengers and the communities with them.
rows.anchor: خطاب للرسل ومن معهم من أممهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surrounding context identifies the polytheists' alleged children of God as the angels, whom the phrase honored servants then describes.
rows.anchor: ظاهر السياق يشهد أنه حكاية قول الوثنيين إن الملائكة أولاده سبحانه فالمراد بالعباد المكرمين الملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their honor is the bestowal of complete servitude: they experience themselves only as servants, as shown by their perfect obedience and freedom from its contrary traits.
rows.anchor: إكرامهم في أنفسهم بالعبودية فلا يشاهدون من أنفسهم إلا أنهم عباد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human servitude is acquired, unlike angelic servitude, while God's gift of honor is bestowed on both; he compares this to the distinction between mukhliṣ and mukhlaṣ.
rows.anchor: الفرق بين كرامة الملائكة والبشر أنها في البشر اكتسابي بخلاف ما في الملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase literally means they never speak before God speaks; their speech follows his.
rows.anchor: لا يسبق فلان فلانا بالقول أي لا يقول شيئا قبل أن يقوله فقوله تبع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Preceding someone in speech can also be an indirect expression for willing first, so the angels' volition follows God's.
rows.anchor: وربما يكنى به عن الإرادة والمشيئة أي إرادته تبع إرادته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fronted phrase by his command marks restriction: they act by his command alone; it does not mean they obey no command from anyone else.
rows.anchor: الظرف متعلق بيعملون قدم عليه لإفادة الحصر أي يعملون بأمره لا بغير أمره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their will and action follow God's will, which is the perfection of servitude because a servant's will and acts belong to the master.
rows.anchor: فهم تابعون لربهم قولا وفعلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage concerns Gog and Magog; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says he treated their identity and the barrier against them fully in his commentary on al-Kahf.
rows.anchor: وقد استوفينا الكلام في معنى يأجوج ومأجوج والسد المضروب دونهم في تفسير سورة الكهف

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One interpretation takes the plural pronoun as humanity and the scene as people emerging from their graves toward the gathering place.
rows.anchor: وقيل ضمير الجمع للناس والمراد خروجهم من قبورهم إلى أرض المحشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects that reading: the preceding opening, approaching promise, circumstantial syntax, and emergence from every height do not fit people leaving graves.
rows.anchor: لا يصدق على الخروج من القبور

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid, who held the grave-emergence interpretation, read الجدث with jīm and the three-dotted thāʾ, meaning grave.
rows.anchor: قرأ صاحب هذا القول وهو مجاهد الجدث بالجيم والثاء المثلثة وهو القبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The true promise that has drawn near is the Hour.
rows.anchor: المراد بالوعد الحق الساعة

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Raghib defines fixed gaze as looking without eyelids blinking; it signals intense attention without distraction and often sudden evil.
rows.anchor: شخوص البصر نظره بحيث لا تطرف أجفانه، كذا ذكره الراغب وهو لازم كمال اهتمام الناظر

words: يَٰوَيْلَنَا قَدْ كُنَّا فِى غَفْلَةٍ مِّنْ هَٰذَا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the Hour suddenly appears, the disbelievers call woe upon themselves and claim they had been made heedless of what they now see.
rows.anchor: حكاية قول الكفار إذا شاهدوا الساعة بغتة فدعوا لأنفسهم بالويل مدعين أنهم غفلوا عما يشاهدونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They correct their excuse by admitting that their heedlessness came from injustice: worldly preoccupations made them forget the afterlife.
rows.anchor: أضربوا عن ذلك بالإعتراف بأن الغفلة لم تنشأ إلا عن ظلمهم بالاشتغال بما ينسي الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He glosses ḥaṣab as fuel for Hell.
rows.anchor: الحصب الوقود

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another reported gloss takes ḥaṣab to mean firewood.
rows.anchor: وقيل الحطب

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A broader proposed sense is anything thrown into a fire.
rows.anchor: وقيل أصله ما يرمى في النار فيكون أعم

words: إِنَّكُمْ وَمَا تَعْبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The objects are idols and statues, not prophets, righteous people, or angels; the next statement about those promised good confirms that exclusion.
rows.anchor: الأصنام والتماثيل التى كانوا يعبدونها دون المعبودين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the Quran often describes idols with rational-person terms, the verse uses ma rather than man to distinguish idols from rational beings who may be worshipped.
rows.anchor: ولم يقل ومن تعبدون - مع تعبيره تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These are judgments addressed on the Day of Resurrection, sentencing idolaters to enter and remain in Hell, rather than a worldly refutation of idol worship.
rows.anchor: الظاهر أن هذه الآيات من خطابات يوم القيامة للكفار وفيها القضاء بدخولهم في النار وخلودهم فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām either emphasizes the transitive construction or means to; the address appears to include both the disbelievers and their gods.
rows.anchor: اللام لتأكيد التعدي أو بمعنى إلى

words: لَوْ كَانَ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ ءَالِهَةً مَّا وَرَدُوهَا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional exposes the worshipped beings' true state, and all of the disbelievers and their gods remain in Hell.
rows.anchor: تفريع وإظهار لحقيقة حال الآلهة التي كانوا يعبدونها لتكون لهم شفعاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zafīr is the sound of breath being drawn back inward, hence its gloss as a donkey's bray.
rows.anchor: الزفير هو الصوت برد النفس إلى داخل ولذا فسر بصوت الحمار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their inability to hear repays their failure to hear truth in worldly life, just as their inability to see repays their refusal to examine God's signs.
rows.anchor: جزاء عدم سمعهم في الدنيا كلمة الحق كما أنهم لا يبصرون جزاء لإعراضهم عن النظر في آيات الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The discourse turns away from addressing the disbelievers and addresses the Prophet to disclose their miserable state to others; plural pronouns now refer only to disbelievers.
rows.anchor: عدول عن خطاب الكفار إلى خطاب النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم إعراضا عن خطابهم ليبين سوء حالهم لغيرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ḥusnā is the feminine of aḥsan used substantively, with an implied promise of salvation or of the Garden.
rows.anchor: الحسنى مؤنث أحسن وهي وصف قائم مقام موصوفه والتقدير العدة أو الموعدة الحسنى بالنجاة أو بالجنة

rows.speaker: من قال
rows.claim: A weaker reading makes the disputant in God the one who misleads whoever takes him as patron, by referring the pronouns back to the relative clause; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī rejects it.
rows.anchor: وأضعف منه قول من قال إن المعنى كتب على هذا الذي يجادل في الله بغير علم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The decree against Iblis extends to his party, descendants, and helpers; their misleading and directing to punishment is, in sum, his act.
rows.anchor: القضاء على إبليس قضاء على قبيله وذريته وأعوانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The subtle juxtaposition of misleading and guiding in the same verse is deliberate.
rows.anchor: ولا يخفى ما في الجمع بين يضله ويهديه في الآية من اللطف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The resurrection at issue is the revivification of the dead and their return to God.
rows.anchor: المراد بالبعث إحياء الموتى والرجوع إلى الله سبحانه وهو ظاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An ʿalaqah is a piece of clotted blood, and a muḍghah is a chewed piece of flesh.
rows.anchor: العلقة القطعة من الدم الجامد

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A reported interpretation takes the terms as fully formed and incompletely formed; this maps to embryo formation associated with the breathing of spirit, and thus to imaging or shaping.
rows.anchor: المخلقة على ما قيل - تامة الخلقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stages demonstrate that resurrection is possible: the observed passage from dead soil through embryo stages to living human removes doubt, so the explanatory phrase appears here.
rows.anchor: لنبين لكم أن البعث ممكن ونزيل الريب عنكم فإن مشاهدة الانتقال من التراب الميت إلى النطفة ثم إلى العلقة

words: وَنُقِرُّ فِى ٱلْأَرْحَامِ مَا نَشَآءُ إِلَىٰٓ أَجَلٍ مُّسَمًّى
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God keeps in the wombs the embryos he wills, without miscarriage, until the full term, then brings them out as children.
rows.anchor: ونقر فيها ما نشاء من الأجنة ولا نسقطه إلى تمام مدة الحمل ثم نخرجكم طفلا

rows.speaker: المجمع
rows.claim: Al-Majmaʿ explains the phrase as bringing children from their mothers' wombs; ṭifl is a young human and its singular can function as a collective, though it may mean each of you as a child.
rows.anchor: قال في المجمع أي نخرجكم من بطون امهاتكم وأنتم أطفال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reaching full strength means the stage when limbs and powers have grown strong.
rows.anchor: والمراد ببلوغ الأشد حال اشتداد الأعضاء والقوى

words: وَمِنكُم مَّن يُتَوَفَّىٰ وَمِنكُم مَّن يُرَدُّ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parallel clauses imply that some die before they are returned to the most decrepit age.
rows.anchor: المقابلة بين الجملتين تدل على تقيد الأولى بما يميزها من الثانية والتقدير ومنكم من يتوفى من قبل أن يرد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lowest age is senility, the most contemptible and weakest stage relative to what came before.
rows.anchor: المراد بأرذل العمر أحقره وأهونه وينطبق على حال الهرم فإنه أرذل الحياه إذا قيس إلى ما قبله

words: لِكَيْلَا يَعْلَمَ مِنۢ بَعْدِ عِلْمٍ شَيْـًٔا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person loses knowledge that matters to the conduct of life as bodily and sensory powers weaken, until nothing of life's most valuable product remains useful.
rows.anchor: أي شيئا يعتد به أرباب الحياة ويبنون عليه حياتهم

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Raghib relates hāmida to a fire that has gone out, land without plants, or dried-up vegetation; the author says ruined or dead earth is close in sense.
rows.anchor: يقال همدت النار طفئت، ومنه أرض هامدة لا نبات فيها

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Raghib says the root denotes vigorous movement; a plant is described as moving when fresh.
rows.anchor: الهز التحريك الشديد يقال هززت الرمح فاهتز واهتز النبات إذا تحرك لنضارته

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Raghib glosses rabā as increasing and rising, the growth of something reared.
rows.anchor: ربا إذا زاد وعلا، قال تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth grows every plant type marked by beauty: pleasing color and an appearance that conveys joy.
rows.anchor: أي وأنبتت الأرض من كل صنف من النبات متصف بالبهجة وهي حسن اللون وظهور السرور فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, zawj may mean a pair opposite to an individual; the Quran thus affirms plant pairing as well as plant life, which experimental sciences have confirmed.
rows.anchor: أو المراد بالزوج ما يقابل الفرد فإن كلامه يثبت للنبات ازدواجا كما يثبت له حياة وقد وافقته العلوم التجريبية اليوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth's production and growth of plants parallels the womb's biological production of a human through the stages from soil to living person.
rows.anchor: للأرض في إنباتها النبات وإنمائها له شأنا يماثل شأن الرحم في إنباته الحيوي للتراب الصائر نطفة ثم علقة ثم مضغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That points to the real creation and management, in origin and continuance, of human beings and plants described in the previous verse.
rows.anchor: ذلك إشارة إلى ما ذكر في الآيه السابقة من خلق الإنسان والنبات وتدبير أمرهما حدوثا وبقاء خلقا وتدبيرا واقعيين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is the Real itself, not an adjective with an omitted noun; he makes every real thing real and sustains the true order, which discloses him as the Real.
rows.anchor: والذي يعطيه السياق أن المراد بالحق نفس الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dead soil becoming a human and dead earth becoming living plants are instances of God's continuing to give life to the dead.
rows.anchor: صيرورة التراب الميت بالانتقال من حال إلى حال إنسانا حيا وكذا صيرورة الأرض الميتة بنزول الماء نباتا حيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creating and sustaining humans and plants depends on the whole cosmic order, so their creation reveals God's power over everything.
rows.anchor: إيجاد الإنسان والنبات وتدبير أمرهما في الحدوث والبقاء مرتبط بما في الكون من وجود أو نظام جار في الوجود

words: وَأَنَّ ٱلسَّاعَةَ ءَاتِيَةٌ لَّا رَيْبَ فِيهَا
وَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَبْعَثُ مَن فِى ٱلْقُبُورِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two clauses about the Hour and resurrection coordinate with the earlier that-clause beginning because God is the Real.
rows.anchor: الجملتان معطوفتان على { أن } في قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The five conclusions are selected to establish resurrection: a wholly real God produces only true acts, so human life cannot end in death without a lasting afterlife, which would make creation futile.
rows.anchor: فإن الحق المحض لا يصدر عنه إلا الفعل الحق دون الباطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The argument parallels verses saying the heavens and earth were created in truth, but this passage proves resurrection from God's own truth, which entails the truth of his acts.
rows.anchor: في مجرى قوله وما خلقنا السماوات والأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To answer the doubt that revival is impossible, he points to God's observed, ongoing conversion of dead soil into living humans and plants as proof of possibility.
rows.anchor: فإحياؤه تعالى الموتى بجعل التراب الميت إنسانا حيا وجعل الأرض الميتة نباتا حيا واقع مستمر مشهود فلا ريب في إمكانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This proof of renewed revival through a prior like act parallels the answer that the one who created bones the first time can revive them.
rows.anchor: في مجرى قوله تعالى قال من يحيي العظام وهي رميم قل يحييها الذي أنشأها أول مرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To answer that possible revival need not occur, he says infinite power makes first and second creation equally easy and cannot suffer incapacity or fatigue.
rows.anchor: فإن القدرة لما كانت غير متناهية كانت نسبتها إلى الإحياء الأول والثاني وما كان سهلا في نفسه أو صعبا على حد سواء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The universal power argument also appears in verses asking whether God was wearied by the first creation and promising that the one who revived earth revives the dead.
rows.anchor: وهذه الجملة أيضا في مجرى قوله تعالى أفعيينا بالخلق الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The three claims in because God through the end of verse 6 are conclusions from verse 5, all serving the stated proof of resurrection in verse 7.
rows.anchor: فهذه أعني ما في قوله تعالى { ذلك بأن الله } إلى آخر الآية

words: وَأَنَّ ٱلسَّاعَةَ ءَاتِيَةٌ لَّا رَيْبَ فِيهَا
وَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَبْعَثُ مَن فِى ٱلْقُبُورِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The concluding verse names both parts of resurrection: the people who will be raised and the Hour in which they are raised.
rows.anchor: ولم تتضمن الآية إلا بعث الأموات والظرف الذي يبعثون فيه فأما الظرف وهو الساعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Hour's coming is not attributed directly to God because it arrives suddenly and is not knowable in advance.
rows.anchor: ولم ينسب إتيانها إلى نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After listing competing groups, the passage says God witnesses and judges them on Judgment Day; even those who refuse outward prostration are inwardly subdued, then their rewards and punishments follow.
rows.anchor: بيان بعد ما ذكر في الآيات السابقة اختلاف الناس واختصامهم في الله سبحانه بين تابع ضال يجادل في الله بغير علم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By contrast with the other communities listed, the believers are those who accepted Muhammad and the Quran.
rows.anchor: المراد بالذين آمنوا بقرينة المقابلة هم الذين آمنوا بمحمد صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم وكتابهم القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Jews are believers in Moses and earlier messengers, with the Torah; Nebuchadnezzar burned it in the seventh century BCE, and Ezra rewrote it after Cyrus conquered Babylon and the exiles returned.
rows.anchor: والذين هادوا هم المؤمنين بموسى من قبله من الرسل الواقفون فيه وكتابهم التوراة وقد أحرقها بخت نصر ملك بابل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because they are distinguished from polytheists, the Sabians here are not star worshippers; they are said to stand between Judaism and Magianism, claim a book from John son of Zechariah, and are called Ṣabī today.
rows.anchor: والصابئون ليس المراد بهم عبدة الكواكب من الوثنية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Christians believe in Jesus and earlier prophets; they revere four canonical Gospels and the Old Testament, while the Quran identifies their revealed book as the Gospel given to Jesus.
rows.anchor: والنصارى هم المؤمنون بالمسيح عيسى ابن مريم عليه السلام ومن قبله من الأنبياء وكتبهم المقدسة الأناجيل الأربعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Magians are commonly identified as Zoroastrians whose Avesta history and revelation date are obscure; Alexander's conquest lost their book and Sasanians rewrote it, complicating knowledge of their doctrine.
rows.anchor: والمجوس المعروف أنهم المؤمنون بزرتشت وكتابهم المقدس أوستا غير أن تاريخ حياته وزمان ظهوره مبهم جدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Magians affirm good and evil principles, Yazdan and Ahriman or light and darkness; they venerate angels and elemental substances, especially fire, yet trace all to Ahura Mazda, creator of all.
rows.anchor: والمسلم أنهم يثبتون لتدبير العالم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The polytheists are idol worshippers; their main organized religions are Sabian idolatry, Brahmanism, and Buddhism, alongside unorganized cults such as Hijaz Arabs and peoples elsewhere, discussed earlier in volume ten.
rows.anchor: والذين أشركوا هم الوثنية عبدة الأصنام

words: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَفْصِلُ بَيْنَهُمْ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's judgment resolves disputes among the religious schools and makes the true party unmistakably distinct from the false.
rows.anchor: فصل القضاء فيما اختلف فيه أصحاب هذه المذاهب واختصموا فينفصل المحق منهم ويتميز من المبطل انفصالا وتميزا لا يستره ساتر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second inna reinforces the sentence after the long separation between the first inna and its predicate.
rows.anchor: وتكرار إن في الآية للتأكيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's witnessing everything explains why his judgment is a judgment in truth.
rows.anchor: تعليل للفصل أنه فصل بالحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address apparently applies to anyone capable of being addressed, and seeing means knowing; alternatively it may address the Prophet specifically and mean inward vision.
rows.anchor: الظاهر أن الخطاب لكل من يرى ويصلح لأن يخاطب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since the list includes nonrational things, prostration means their ontological abasement under God's majesty and dominion.
rows.anchor: وتعميم السجدة لمثل الشمس والقمر والنجوم والجبال من غير أولى العقل دليل على أن المراد بها السجدة التكوينية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This ontological submission includes every human, believer and disbeliever, since no one is exempt from existential subjection.
rows.anchor: شاملا لنوع الإنسان من مؤمن وكافر

words: مَن فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَن فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though heaven and earth themselves are not separately listed, all upper and lower creatures, rational and nonrational, continually submit to God necessarily in their existence.
rows.anchor: وعدم ذكر نفس السماوات والأرض في جملة الساجدين مع شمول الحكم لهما في الواقع يعطي أن معنى الكلام أن المخلوقات العلوية والسفلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because all humans were already included in ontological submission, this many prostrate in a second, voluntary and ritual sense by falling to the ground to express servanthood.
rows.anchor: وإسناد السجود إلى كثير من الناس بعد شموله في الجملة السابقة لجميعهم دليل على أن المراد بهذا السجود نوع آخر من السجود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This contrasting phrase stands for those who refuse to prostrate; naming their deserved punishment instead shows it as the consequence of their own action and prepares for the humiliation that follows.
rows.anchor: المقابلة بينه وبين سابقه تعطي أن معناه

words: وَمَن يُهِنِ ٱللَّهُ فَمَا لَهُۥ مِن مُّكْرِمٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By God's will, refusal to prostrate brings punishment and an abasement never followed by honor; all good belongs to God, and no one else can give what he withholds.
rows.anchor: وهو إهانة ليس بعده إكرام أبدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This phrase is an indirect assertion of universal power and explains the punishment and irreversible humiliation of those arrogant toward prostration.
rows.anchor: كناية عن عموم القدرة وتعليل لما تقدمه من حديث إثباته العذاب للمستكبرين عن السجود له وإهانتهم إهانة لا إكرام بعده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage connects God's final separation of disputants to the contrast between universal created submission and humans who either worship openly or arrogantly refuse and are humiliated.
rows.anchor: ومن هنا يظهر أن للآية اتصالا بما قبلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two disputing parties are the groups previously indicated by God's separation of religious communities and by the contrast between many prostrating and many condemned.
rows.anchor: إلى القبيلين الذين دل عليهما قوله سابقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All scattered religions reduce to two parties, truth and falsehood; without that binary, their many creeds could not be contained in two sides.
rows.anchor: ويعلم من حصر المختلفين على كثرة أديانهم ومذاهبهم في خصمين اثنين أنهم جميعا منقسمون إلى محق ومبطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He praises خصمان اختصموا: there are two camps despite their many individual doctrines, so neither خصوم اختصموا nor dual خصمان اختصما conveys the point as well.
rows.anchor: حيث لم يقل خصوم اختصموا ولم يقل خصمان اختصما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their dispute concerns how they describe God's lordship; doctrinal differences ultimately return to descriptions of his attributes and acts.
rows.anchor: وقد جعل اختصامهم في ربهم أي أنهم اختلفوا في وصف ربوبيته تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The true party describes God with fitting names, attributes, and acts, believes in them, and acts accordingly as faithful workers of righteousness.
rows.anchor: فهم بين من يصف ربه بما يستحقه من الأسماء والصفات وما يليق به من الأفعال فيؤمن بما وصف وهو الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The false party assigns God a partner or child, attributes creation to nature or time, denies prophethood or a messenger, or rejects an essential truth of religion, thereby concealing truth.
rows.anchor: ومن لا يصفه بما يستحقه من الأسماء والصفات كمن يثبت له شريكا أو ولدا فينفي وحدانيته أو يسند الصنع والإيجاد إلى الطبيعة أو الدهر

words: فَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ قُطِّعَتْ لَهُمْ ثِيَابٌ مِّن نَّارٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After judgment the passage begins the two parties' recompense with the unbelievers, whose clothing is cut from fire and whose heads are doused with boiling water.
rows.anchor: ثم شرع في جزاء الخصمين وبين عاقبة أمر كل منهما بعد فصل القضاء
